title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Two Issues in Handling Cases Concerning Redemption of Pawned Houses During the Socialist Transformation of Private Houses

articles.content_en: 1. When handling cases concerning the redemption of pawned houses in the socialist transformation of private houses, the People's Court shall still refer to the "Opinions on Handling Issues of Pawned Houses in the Reform of Private Houses" (Document No. 105 (65) Guo Fang Ju Zi of the State Administration of Housing) for handling; however, such issues of house pawns are relatively complex and involve strong policy considerations. Local courts may, in the course of enforcement, handle them differently according to specific circumstances. If the pawned house was not redeemed before the transformation and the title was transferred to the State during the transformation, redemption shall not be allowed after the transformation; if the pawned house was not transformed and the title was not transferred to the State, the case shall be handled in accordance with the provision in Document No. 105 (65) Guo Fang Ju Zi that "from now on, pawned houses shall generally still be handled according to the pawn relationship"①, the provision of Article (58) of the "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of Civil Policies and Laws" (Document No. 112 (84) Fa Ban Zi of the Supreme People's Court), and the interpretations of this Article given by the Supreme People's Court in recent years.

2. The second paragraph of Article (58) of the "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of Civil Policies and Laws" (Document No. 112 (84) Fa Ban Zi of the Supreme People's Court) stipulates: "If the pawn period expires and it has been overdue for ten years, or if the pawn period is not specified and thirty years have elapsed without redemption, it shall in principle be deemed an absolute sale." When handling dispute cases involving pawned houses that have not been transformed, if the redemption period specified above has been exceeded, the People's Court shall confirm that the title to the house belongs to the pawnee; if the redemption period has not been exceeded, the court shall permit the pawner to redeem the house.
This is a reply.
September 8, 1988
① Item 1 of Article 1 of that document stipulates: Pawned houses are different from houses that are rented out. If a pawned house is included in the transformation, nominally it is the pawner who is transformed, but in reality it is the pawnee who is transformed. Therefore, from now on, pawned houses shall generally still be handled according to the pawn relationship.
